title: Closing a Forwarded Matter — Outcomes, Charges and Client Reporting (Legal Forwarding Agreements)
content:
**Training note for client services staff on the Legal Forwarding Agreements.** A forwarded matter ends with one recorded closure, carrying its closing date and one of five outcomes: paid, settled, dismissed, recalled or uncollectible.

## The rule

A matter closes:

- **as paid or settled** when the debt is resolved, after which a satisfaction of judgment is filed within the programme's satisfaction filing period in calendar days;
- **as dismissed** when the client asks for a filed suit to be dismissed, charging the programme's dismissal fee;
- **as recalled** when the client recalls the account, charging the programme's recall-after-suit fee — a percentage of the balance due at recall — if a suit was filed, and billing the matter's costs where the programme bills costs on recalled matters;
- **as uncollectible** when the programme's uncollectible closure period, in months, passes after judgment with no recovery.

A matter is closed once. The client receives a status report at every status report interval of the programme, counted in calendar days, while a matter is open, and court-awarded attorney fees are shared by the programme's attorney share of those fees.

## Outcomes at a glance

| Outcome | What brings it about | Charge or step attached |
|---|---|---|
| Paid | the debt is resolved | satisfaction of judgment filed within the programme's period |
| Settled | the debt is resolved | satisfaction of judgment filed within the programme's period |
| Dismissed | the client asks for a filed suit to be dismissed | the programme's dismissal fee |
| Recalled | the client recalls the account | the recall-after-suit fee on the balance due at recall, if a suit was filed; the matter's costs billed where the programme bills them |
| Uncollectible | the programme's period in months passes after judgment with no recovery | — |

## Questions and answers

**Q1. A client recalls an account on which suit was filed, with a balance due of $3000.00 at recall, under a programme with a 15 percent recall-after-suit fee and costs billed on recall. What is charged?** (Hypothetical figures.) The recall-after-suit fee is 15 percent of $3000.00, that is $450.00, and the matter's costs are billed to the client because the programme bills costs on recalled matters.

**Q2. On which balance is the recall-after-suit fee figured?** On the balance due on the account at the time of recall.

**Q3. Can a matter that has already been closed as settled be closed again as recalled?** No. A matter is closed once.

**Q4. After a matter closes as paid, what follows?** A satisfaction of judgment is filed within the programme's satisfaction filing period, in calendar days.

**Q5. When does a matter become uncollectible?** When the programme's uncollectible closure period, in months, passes after judgment with no recovery. A recovery within that period means the condition is not met.

**Q6. How often does the client hear about an open matter?** It receives a status report at the programme's interval in calendar days for as long as the matter is open.

**Q7. Who receives court-awarded attorney fees?** They are shared according to the programme's share of court-awarded attorney fees kept by the attorney.
